name: inc-2213
incidentInput: Customers are seeing errors at checkout and the site feels slow. Started maybe 15–20 min ago.

input.summary: Likely cause: CFG-502 raised inventory-service DB_POOL_MAX 20->80 at 13:52 (6 replicas, budget 120->480), over-committing orders-db (max 400, no pooler). Inventory holds ~320 connections (LOG-076, LOG-121), total 397/400, starving orders-service (too many clients, Hikari timeouts), causing checkout 5xx and latency. Confidence fairly high but not human-confirmed.

hypotheses.statement: CFG-502 inventory pool increase exhausted orders-db connections, starving orders-service and breaking checkout
hypotheses.reasoning: Onset 13:55 matches the config 3 min earlier. Inventory uses ~320 of 397 connections. The payments rollback and retry-flag change did not fix the 5xx (ALR-014). Payments latency and the reporting CPU spike are secondary: retries and the hourly rollup.
Its error rate and processor latency are unchanged. The rollback did not clear the errors. The latency rise came from checkout retries.

nextActions.action: Reconcile the 14 orders where the card was charged but no order was confirmed, and release the duplicate holds
Put PgBouncer in front of orders-db (INC-2041 action item) and add a guardrail on the pool-size budget
Re-enable the checkout flag payments_retry_on_timeout only after recovery is verified

openQuestions: Did the inventory owner intend CFG-502, and why was it made?
Are there duplicate charges or lost orders? Payments and support can check.
Does the 14:02 reporting rollup add load? Reporting owner to confirm.
input.impact: Onset 13:55. Checkout errors peaked at 7.9% and p99 at 5.1s. Orders error rate peaked at 10.3%. CUST-001: 87 tickets by 14:30. CUST-002: 14 reports of cards charged with no order confirmation. Search and browsing are unaffected (CUST-004).
input.stakeholderUpdate: Customers are hitting errors when placing orders, and some have been charged without getting a confirmation. The likely cause is a recent configuration change that lets one internal service use too many database connections, which leaves checkout short of them. We plan to revert that change and then reconcile the affected orders. We will send the next update after the revert.

input.rationale: Config-driven connection over-commitment is well supported by the metrics and logs.
